title: Propensity Scores, Matching & Weighting
interviewAnswer: The propensity score is the probability of treatment given observed covariates. Matching or inverse-probability weighting can balance observed confounders, but cannot repair unmeasured confounding or poor overlap.
why: Propensity Scores, Matching & Weighting appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: The propensity score is the probability of treatment given observed covariates. Matching or inverse-probability weighting can balance observed confounders, but cannot repair unmeasured confounding or poor overlap. Assess covariate balance after adjustment. Extreme weights increase variance. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Weight observational treatment records so measured pre-treatment characteristics resemble a randomized comparison.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
